subject: Request: enclave penetration scope, evidence, and remediation status

Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Enclave penetration details & remediations for Private deployment

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing our SIG questionnaire and the procurement security review flagged a need for more granular penetration test evidence specific to the Private (customer VPC) deployment we evaluated last month. Two asks from our InfoSec team:

1) A short explanation of the enclave boundary assumptions you used during your most recent internal penetration test (what you consider in-scope vs out-of-scope for a customer VPC/private deployment).
2) The redacted penetration test report (or executive summary) plus an itemized remediation tracker showing which findings apply to private deployments and their current status.

Our legal team also wants to confirm whether any external network-facing proofs-of-concept were executed inside customer VPCs or only in Redwood-managed test environments.

Can you confirm a timeline for delivery — we ideally need the executive summary and scope notes by EOD Wednesday (2026-02-11) to keep the procurement slot.

Best,
Carlos Ruiz
Senior InfoSec Manager
FinServ Corp

Carlos —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front:
- We do not execute customer-targeted exploits inside customer-controlled VPCs without explicit, written authorization and a signed Statement of Work that includes live testing.
- Our standard internal penetration test for Private deployments is carried out in an instrumented staging environment that mirrors the customer VPC topology (network ACLs, subnets, routing, and IAM roles), and we annotate which findings would materially affect a customer enclave.

I'll loop in Laura (security lead for Private) and Stephanie (remediation owner) who will provide the redacted executive summary, a brief boundary assumptions write-up, and the remediation tracker. We should be able to deliver the requested artifacts by EOD Wednesday.

Action items I will do now:
- Confirm the precise scope you want redacted (PII vs exploit PoCs)
- Provide signed attestation that no live exploitation occurred in customer VPCs without SOW authorization

Rishi Malhotra

Carlos —

Sharing the requested scope and a short boundary summary here (attached: RI-2025-pen-report-redacted.pdf, enclave-boundary-diagram.png). Key points: 

1) Boundary assumptions for Private (customer VPC) testing-
- In-scope: Redwood-managed inference runtime components (model serving nodes, KG cache layer, control-plane agents) that would run inside the customer's VPC when deploying Redwood Private; customer-provided ingress/load balancers and their configuration when explicitly part of the customer deployment.
- Out-of-scope: Customer-managed data stores not connected to the inference service, third-party services hosted within the VPC that are not referenced in the deployment manifest, and any tenant's unrelated workloads.

2) Test environment practices-
- Tests were executed in a Redwood staging environment that mirrors network topology and IAM roles but uses synthetic customer data. We maintain a mapping document that ties staging instances to customer VPC configuration when customers request a bespoke test.
- We do not execute unauthorised active exploit chains inside customer-managed VPCs. Any live testing on a customer's VPC requires a one-off SOW and customer-signed approval.

3) PoC handling and redaction policy-
- Raw PoC exploit code and screenshots are redacted in the executive PDF; we include a descriptive reproduction path and risk rating for each finding. PoCs involving customer data are sanitized.

Attached I included the redacted report and a boundary diagram. The remediation tracker is still updating; Stephanie will share the latest status with specific finding IDs and ETA for fixes.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Hi Carlos / team —

Per Laura's note, attaching the remediation tracker (remediation-tracker-2026-02-11.xlsx). Summary status for items that map to Private deployments: 
- High (3 open): two auth bypass vectors (mitigations scheduled, hotfix in staging), one TLS termination misconfiguration (patch rolling 2/12).
- Medium (5 open): misc hardening (config templates + IaC PRs ready).
- Low (2 open): informational recommendations (completed).

For your procurement timeline: we can provide a signed attestation that the listed High items are being actively remediated and provide a targeted verification snapshot after the hotfix deploy (ETA 2026-02-13). If you need a re-test inside a customer environment, we'll need an SOW and explicit authorization.

Let me know if you want individual finding IDs broken down by which Redwood staging component they map to — happy to export that slice.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
